anomalies.observed: On the schematic, J1 pin 26 is connected to the +3V3 power symbol, while J2 pin 26 is labelled PIN26. The two bus connectors therefore do not present the same net on pin 26.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that J1 and J2 have identical nets on both connectors for pass-through operation. Pin 26 should not be tied to +3V3 on only one connector; it should carry the same bus net on both J1 and J2.

evidence.quote: J1 pin 26 has a +3V3 power symbol; J2 pin 26 is labelled PIN26 (sheet m5-pantilt.kicad_sch)
J1 / J2 ... identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through).

anomalies.impact: Bus pin 26 on one connector is driven by the +3V3 rail instead of the intended pass-through net. This breaks stacking/pass-through and can short +3V3 into a GPIO bus pin, potentially causing malfunction or damage to a connected M5Stack Core or module.

parsed.summary: The drawing appears to contain a pass-through error: J1 pin 26 is tied to +3V3 whereas J2 pin 26 is labelled PIN26, contradicting the specification that J1 and J2 carry identical nets.
